subject: ventures/jwt-security-check
professional: an application security engineer who triages JWTs during a pentest or code review. What they check first: alg none in every spelling and in its canonical empty-signature form (RFC 7519 6.1), algorithm confusion and an expected-algorithm allow-list (RFC 8725 2.1, 3.1), embedded/referenced keys (jwk, jku, x5u, x5c), kid injection, weak HMAC secrets (RFC 8725 3.5, the jwt.io 'your-256-bit-secret' token), exp/nbf handling per RFC 7519 4.1.4-4.1.5, explicit typing and crit (RFC 8725 3.11, RFC 7515 4.1.11), and that the tool itself is safe to paste an attacker's token into

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with an independent Python decoder and HMAC-SHA256 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5b35c5c9-389a-5954-9742-ad2b53d8c6ff/scratchpad/jwt/ref.py, base64.urlsafe_b64decode + hmac) and ran calc.mjs on the same tokens via /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5b35c5c9-389a-5954-9742-ad2b53d8c6ff/scratchpad/jwt/run.mjs with now=2026-11-13T00:00:00Z. Right: the jwt.io HS256 example decodes to the same header/payload and gets missing-exp (high), missing-aud, missing-iss; the RFC 7519 3.1 example (HMAC verifies with the RFC 7515 A.1 key) decodes identically, exp 1300819380 = 2011-03-22T18:43:00Z is flagged expired, missing-iat and missing-aud, iss present so not flagged; alg ' none' and 'None' are caught when a signature segment is present; a 0.5-hour-future nbf is flagged. Wrong: (1) the canonical unsecured JWT from RFC 7519 6.1 (eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.. with an empty third segment, the exact shape of the alg:none attack) returns ok:false and a single 'invalid-structure' finding whose text says an empty signature 'is only valid for an explicitly unsigned alg none token', with no alg-none finding, although the header decoded to {alg:none}; (2) a kid of ; is echoed raw into the finding detail and the page renders it with innerHTML: in headless Chrome against a copy of index.html the onerror handler ran (body got data-pwned=yes); (3) exp exactly equal to now is not flagged expired, though RFC 7519 4.1.4 says the current time MUST be before exp; (4) a header segment of length 4n+1 decodes silently, where Python's base64 rejects it.
evidence.completeness: Claimed checks (README 'What gets flagged', VENTURE.yaml description) exercised with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5b35c5c9-389a-5954-9742-ad2b53d8c6ff/scratchpad/jwt/probe.mjs: alg none (works with a non-empty signature segment; misfiled as invalid structure in the canonical empty-signature form), missing alg (works), jwk/jku/x5u/x5c (works, one finding each), HS* plus key hint (works), kid ../ and SQL metacharacters (works), missing/non-numeric/expired exp (works), excessive lifetime 24h/30d tiers (works, only when iat is present: a 99-year exp with no iat is not flagged), missing/future iat (works), future nbf (works), missing aud/iss (works), sensitive field names (works for the exact names in the regex; user_password and client_secret are not flagged), copy summary, example token, usage opt-out (present in index.html). No stubs or TODOs. Every claimed check exists and fires on its happy-path input.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/jwt-security-check && node --test '*.test.mjs': 67 tests, 67 pass, 0.15 s. Seeded 6 mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 5 caught (exp comparison, clock-skew constant, 30-day tier, nbf comparison, base64 bit arithmetic); 1 survived (dropping the backslash branch of the kid path-traversal regex, calc.mjs:220). The suite does not catch either real defect: calc.test.mjs:62 asserts the empty-signature error and so enshrines the alg-none misfiling, and page.test.mjs checks markup but never that a finding's text is escaped before innerHTML.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (413 lines), index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Small, dependency-free, pure functions with clear comments, own base64url decoder that runs in browser and node. Defects: index.html:145 builds each finding with innerHTML and interpolates f.detail, which contains the token's own kid (calc.mjs:237); for a security tool whose users paste suspicious tokens this is a stored-in-the-token XSS on the shared marisstella.app origin. parseJwt treats an empty signature as a parse error before the alg is considered (calc.mjs:122); base64UrlToBytes does not reject a 4n+1 length (calc.mjs:39); a non-string alg such as 123 produces no finding (calc.mjs:155).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'never verifies a signature / never asks for a key' (calc.mjs has no crypto; page.test.mjs:51); 'nothing uploaded, no network requests' (index.html script imports only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs, no fetch); no-warranty, privacy and best-effort paragraphs on README and page (page.test.mjs:51-67); 'a clean result is not a guarantee' stated on page and in summaryText. Not backed: index.html:98 (and the FAQ JSON-LD at :14) 'This tool flags it [alg none] as high severity whenever it appears' and vs-eyeballing-the-payload.html:42 'Flags it as high severity every time' are false for the RFC 7519 6.1 token, which gets only an invalid-structure finding that never says alg none is the problem. llms.txt:5 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' is generator boilerplate (platform/ci/gen_llms_txt.py:48) that does not describe a token checker. The served page https://marisstella.app/jwt-security-check/ could not be loaded from this session (curl: CONNECT 403; WebFetch: host not resolvable), so no URL defect was filed about the github.io links in source llms.txt (the build rewrites hosts).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an AppSec engineer pastes a captured token from a target. It decodes quickly and the checklist of header/claim findings is a reasonable first-minute triage, with honest caveats. Gaps hit in the first hour: the attacker-crafted alg none token (empty signature) is reported as malformed instead of as alg none; pasting a hostile token with an HTML kid executes script in the page; the most common real finding in pentests, a guessable HMAC secret, is never checked (the jwt.io token signed with 'your-256-bit-secret' gets no key finding; jwt_tool and hashcat mode 16500 do this offline with no user key); no typ/crit checks; JWE tokens (5 segments, RFC 7516, valid JWTs per RFC 7519) are rejected as malformed.
evidence.domain: Compared against RFC 7519 (4.1.4 exp, 4.1.5 nbf, 6.1 unsecured JWT), RFC 7515 (4.1.11 crit), RFC 8725 (2.1 alg none, 2.3 weak symmetric keys, 3.1 algorithm verification, 3.5 key entropy, 3.7 kid/claims validation, 3.11 explicit typing) and the OWASP JWT Cheat Sheet. Matches: alg none case-insensitive, embedded key headers, kid path/SQL shapes, exp/iat/nbf semantics with a 5-minute iat skew, aud/iss as audience confusion (RFC 8725 2.8). Departures: the canonical RFC 7519 6.1 unsecured JWT is not identified as alg none; exp == now treated as valid against 4.1.4's 'MUST be before'; no weak-HMAC-secret check (RFC 8725 3.5); no explicit typing or crit check; excessive lifetime only computed from iat, never from exp minus now; the alg-confusion check only fires when the header carries a key hint, which the real RS256->HS256 attack token does not (stated as a shape check, so a limit rather than an error).

defects.what: XSS: the kid header value is interpolated into the finding detail (calc.mjs:237) and the page renders details with innerHTML, so a token whose kid is ; runs script on the marisstella.app origin when pasted (confirmed in headless Chrome); a security tool's users paste hostile tokens by design

the canonical alg none token (RFC 7519 6.1, empty signature segment) is reported only as 'invalid-structure', never as alg-none, because parseJwt fails on the empty signature before the alg is checked; calc.test.mjs:62 enshrines the behaviour
page claims alg none is flagged as high severity 'whenever it appears' / 'every time'; false for the empty-signature form
no weak-HMAC-secret check (RFC 8725 3.5): the jwt.io token signed with 'your-256-bit-secret' gets no key finding, though an offline dictionary check needs no user key
exp exactly equal to now is not flagged expired; RFC 7519 4.1.4 requires now to be before exp
excessive lifetime is only computed from exp - iat; a token with a 99-year exp and no iat is not flagged
base64url segments of length 4n+1 are decoded silently instead of rejected
a non-string alg (e.g. 123) produces no finding
no explicit-typing (typ, RFC 8725 3.11) or crit (RFC 7515 4.1.11) checks; JWE tokens (5 segments) are rejected as malformed although RFC 7519 allows JWE JWTs
a mutant dropping the backslash branch of the kid path-traversal regex survives; no test for ..\ or for escaping of finding text
sensitive-field regex is anchored to exact names, so user_password and client_secret are not flagged
llms.txt says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', generator boilerplate that does not describe a token checker

verdict: A clean, private JWT decoder whose base64url decoding and claim checks agree with the RFC 7519 3.1 example and the jwt.io token, and whose tests catch 5 of 6 seeded bugs. It does not meet the bar: the canonical alg none token from RFC 7519 6.1 (empty signature, the exact attack shape) is reported as malformed rather than as alg none, contradicting the page's 'flags it whenever it appears'; a hostile kid is rendered through innerHTML and executes script, which a security tool that invites pasting attacker tokens cannot ship; and it never checks for a weak HMAC secret, the finding an AppSec engineer most often gets from a JWT. Smaller gaps: exp == now treated as valid, no lifetime check without iat, no typ/crit checks.
